# Baking sourdough bread

## Feeding the starter

A sourdough starter is a living culture of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria.
Feed the starter with equal weights of flour and water every day, and keep it
at room temperature until it doubles in size and smells pleasantly sour.

## Hydration and shaping

Dough hydration is the ratio of water to flour. A high hydration dough of
around 75 percent gives an open crumb but is sticky and harder to shape.
Use wet hands and a bench scraper, and build surface tension with gentle folds.

## Baking in a Dutch oven

Preheat the oven and the Dutch oven to 250 C. Score the loaf with a razor
blade, bake covered for twenty minutes to trap steam, then uncover and bake
until the crust is deep brown. Let the bread cool before slicing.
